resources.string: MobilityLens
Input and Interaction
Phones depend on touch, voice, and gestures but not with a mouse and keyboard and screen space for input controls is limited.
Design large, easy to tap buttons and avoid assuming precise pointer input like hover states.
Screen Size, Orientation, and Density
Mobile screens are small, vary widely in resolution, and can rotate between portrait and landscape at any time.
Use flexible layouts that change to different screen sizes and handle rotation gracefully instead of a single fixed layout.
Lifecycle and Resource Constraints
Mobile apps can be paused, backgrounded, or killed by the system at any time to save battery and memory.
Save important state before the app is interrupted so users do not lose progress when switching apps.
Context Awareness
Phones have GPS, accelerometer, and camera that let apps respond to the users real-world surroundings.
Use location or sensor data perfectly to make the app more useful while asking permission only when truly needed.
Usage Patterns
Mobile sessions are typically short and frequent, often used in brief moments throughout the day rather than long sittings.
Design for quick task completion and let users pick up where they left off after a short interruption.
Security and Privacy Expectations
Phones store personal data and are frequently lost or stolen, so users expect stronger protection of their information.
Request only the permissions and data the app truly needs, and avoid storing sensitive data unnecessarily.
